questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had Italian in high school, and always wanted to try to live there. So studying there was perfect opportunity for me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, because you can always write the office and get i quick response. But italy is a bit late with information, so patience is key

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Got a mail about registration for classes and how to get proof of attendance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: More help could have been more welcoming, but I figures it all out without any problems. But very happy I knew other people in same situation as me

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Spotahome which worked fine, and had sort of a security deposit, ensuring that neither me or my landlord got scammed the first month. My friend found it, so not sure how easy it was. Depends on how picky you are I guess and economic situation of course. I stayed in a room with my own bathroom, but shared kitchen and apartment with five others

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is not that important to live centrally, but try to stay close to a metro line. Every neighborhood has something nice to offer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can first registre 2 weeks before class starts, but it is possible to try classes and change them in the first weeks. For me it was a bit of a puzzle to take different classes, without them overlaping to get my 30 ects. But the classes has both attending and non-attending exam, which also gives flexibility

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course information ind the course cataloge, you can write the professors and the erasmus office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was succesful, except some classes overlaped

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that classes can overlap, and look at the syllabus and the exam form, before registering. Know that you can do both attending and non attending classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was different for each course, but overall my experience is that you can take master classes even though you are at a BA level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More presentations. But less reading homework. Not that much class discussion. Mostly lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Digital Society
Languages of the media
Value Change and global society
Global Social Dynamic

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked Value Change, because it was a small class, which made it easy to interact. The professor was good, and i liked the written exam.
I would also recomend Christopher Andersson classes, he is american which make him easy to understand. The italian accent can be a bit difficult at times. But be aware that the courses is not at very high level, and more generel topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Small trips, lots of aperol, fridays and saturdays at Alcatraz

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee, wine, beers, olive oil, pasta and other local foods. Public transport

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN - but I did not really try any

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Drink coffee everyday, it is cheap and culture. Take small trips to other cities,  I went to Bergamo, Parma, Bologna and Rapallo. 
Go to Alcatraz, huge night club. Try Bar Picchio, lots of young students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take small trips to other cities,  I went to Bergamo, Parma, Bologna, Varenna (como) and Rapallo.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: ESN events and international students. Just talk, people are very nice

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some students were whispering during class and used their phones a lot. The italians are more loose and less structual, like professors are late for exams

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aperitivo :)) People being at bars all day, coffe during the day and aperitvo in the evening. Cheap coffee and wine. And all of their food. Every city has a local specialty

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy! 
Be prepared for a different way of studying
Look at exams before signing up for a course

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will get use to the more relaxed culture

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to integrate in a different culture and univsersity. Meeting new people. Having a new social circel, and hanging out with the same people every week. Not having a job, and just lve

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The teachers english. And they do the exams very differently than at Pædagogik, with more written exams in person. But it was okay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
